scope: All 39 chapters; named cast, distinctive recurring unnamed figures, and named cultural references. English original and modern edition bindings.
anchorPolicy: Snapshot after means paragraph END, not paragraph start. At first mention, supply useful baseline identity: ordinary family relationships, occupation, and setting may be identified before their explanatory paragraph. Do not reveal concealed identities, later relationship changes, actions, motives, revelations, or outcomes. Keep stable identity in later subtitles. Story role has its own release gate.

snapshots.name: Edna Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: The novel’s central character; Léonce’s wife
snapshots.body: Edna Pontellier is the novel’s central character, married to Léonce and the mother of Raoul and Etienne. She has returned from bathing with Robert, who stays to talk while her husband goes out.

snapshots.name: Edna Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: The novel’s central character; Léonce’s wife
snapshots.body: The young mother spending the summer at Grand Isle. She is less at ease than the other guests with their intimate conversation. Her affectionate friend Adèle often brings her sewing to sit with her.

snapshots.name: Edna Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: The novel’s central character; Léonce’s wife
snapshots.body: Usually reserved, she has begun sharing memories and feelings with Adèle, her friend from the cottages. She recalls a childhood in Kentucky and a marriage that offered security without fulfilling her romantic dreams.

snapshots.name: Edna Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: The novel’s central character; Léonce’s wife
snapshots.body: The young mother whose summer at Grand Isle we follow. She has just learned to swim alone, feeling an exhilarating freedom before a sudden fear sent her back toward the shore.

snapshots.name: Edna Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: The novel’s central character; Léonce’s wife
snapshots.body: After her first independent swim, she has refused her husband’s demand that she come indoors. She is surprised by the strength of her own resistance.

snapshots.name: Edna Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: The novel’s central character; Léonce’s wife
snapshots.body: Robert’s sudden departure has left her distressed. She recognizes her feelings for the young man who spent so much of the summer with her as an infatuation.

snapshots.name: Edna Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: The novel’s central character; Léonce’s wife
snapshots.body: Back in New Orleans, she has abandoned her usual reception afternoons and begun working seriously at painting. Her husband is bewildered by her refusal to organize her days around the household.

snapshots.name: Edna Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: The novel’s central character; Léonce’s wife
snapshots.body: She plans to leave the large family house for a small rented home nearby. Money of her own, racing winnings, and sales of her sketches will support the move. She wants greater independence from her husband.

snapshots.name: Edna Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: The novel’s central character; Léonce’s wife
snapshots.body: She has responded passionately to Arobin’s kiss, yet recognizes that she does not love him. Her love remains fixed on Robert, the companion who left for Mexico.

snapshots.name: Edna Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: The novel’s central character; Léonce’s wife
snapshots.body: She has established herself in the small home she calls the pigeon house. A visit to her children in Iberville brought intense affection and a painful farewell; back in the city, she is alone again.

snapshots.name: Edna Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: The novel’s central character; Léonce’s wife
snapshots.body: She and Robert have kissed and spoken openly of their love. She rejects his idea that her husband could give her away, insisting that she chooses for herself.

snapshots.name: Edna Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: The novel’s central character; Léonce’s wife
snapshots.body: After staying beside Adèle during childbirth, she returned expecting Robert to be waiting. Instead, she found his farewell note and lay awake through the night.

snapshots.name: Edna Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: The novel’s central character; Léonce’s wife
snapshots.body: She has returned alone to the nearly deserted holiday cottages. After speaking with Victor and Mariequita, she sets off toward the beach before dinner.

snapshots.name: Edna Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: The novel’s central character; Léonce’s wife
snapshots.body: She has swum out alone from Grand Isle. As exhaustion overtakes her and the shore recedes, her thoughts return to her children, the people she has loved, and sounds from childhood.

introduction.name: Edna Pontellier
introduction.subtitle: The novel’s central character; Léonce’s wife
introduction.body: Edna Pontellier is the novel’s central character. She and her husband, Léonce, have two young sons and are spending the summer at Grand Isle.

snapshots.name: Mr. Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s husband; a New Orleans broker
snapshots.body: Léonce is Edna Pontellier’s husband and a New Orleans broker. Their two young sons are playing nearby while he tries to read his newspaper at Grand Isle.

snapshots.name: Léonce Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s husband; a New Orleans broker
snapshots.body: The man with the newspaper at the opening. His wife calls him Léonce. He went to Klein’s hotel while she stayed on the porch with Robert.

snapshots.name: Léonce Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s husband; a New Orleans broker
snapshots.body: He criticized Edna’s care of the boys after returning late at night, then went back to his business in the city. His gifts of treats prompted the other women to praise him as a husband.

snapshots.name: Léonce Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s husband; a New Orleans broker
snapshots.body: Back in New Orleans, he is upset that Edna missed her reception afternoon. He connects these social obligations with his business interests and has left their unsatisfactory dinner to eat at his club.

snapshots.name: Léonce Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s husband; a New Orleans broker
snapshots.body: Concerned by Edna’s changed behavior, he has consulted the family doctor. He plans a business trip to New York; the doctor advises him to give her space rather than oppose her.

snapshots.name: Léonce Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s husband; a New Orleans broker
snapshots.body: He has left for New York, planning to attend Edna’s sister’s wedding on the way. The boys have gone to their grandmother in Iberville, leaving Edna alone in the city.

snapshots.name: Léonce Pontellier
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s husband; a New Orleans broker
snapshots.body: From New York, he objects to Edna’s move into a smaller house. He arranges renovations and announces a proposed trip abroad, giving society another explanation for the family home’s closure.

introduction.name: Léonce Pontellier
introduction.subtitle: Edna’s husband; a New Orleans broker
introduction.body: Léonce Pontellier is the husband of Edna, the novel’s central character. They have two young sons, Raoul and Etienne.

snapshots.name: Robert Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Madame Lebrun’s elder son
snapshots.body: Robert is Madame Lebrun’s elder son, home for the summer from his work in New Orleans. He has returned from the beach with Edna and stays to talk when Léonce goes out.

snapshots.name: Robert Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Madame Lebrun’s elder son
snapshots.body: He works in New Orleans and spends his summers with his mother, who runs the holiday cottages. He enjoys talking with Edna and has long talked about going to Mexico to seek his fortune.

snapshots.name: Robert Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Madame Lebrun’s elder son
snapshots.body: He spends much of his time with Edna. Devoting himself to a woman each summer is a familiar habit here, but Edna is unsure how seriously to take his joking about earlier attachments.

snapshots.name: Robert Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Madame Lebrun’s elder son
snapshots.body: Adèle has asked him to leave Edna alone, fearing that she might take his attentions seriously. He reacted sharply, then apologized and suggested that he was the one who needed warning.

snapshots.name: Robert Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Madame Lebrun’s elder son
snapshots.body: When Edna felt unwell in church, he brought her to a welcoming island home and stayed while she slept. They spent the afternoon together and returned by boat after nightfall.

snapshots.name: Robert Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Madame Lebrun’s elder son
snapshots.body: He has abruptly left Grand Isle to seek work in Mexico. Edna was hurt that he kept his decision from her, and their farewell was strained.

snapshots.name: Robert Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Madame Lebrun’s elder son
snapshots.body: He is in Mexico. Although he has not written directly to Edna, his letter to the pianist asks repeatedly about her and requests that she be played a favorite piece of music.

snapshots.name: Robert Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Madame Lebrun’s elder son
snapshots.body: A letter says he will return very soon, without giving a reason. The pianist believes that he loves Edna and has been trying to forget her; this is her interpretation of his silence.

snapshots.name: Robert Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Madame Lebrun’s elder son
snapshots.body: Edna has met him by chance at the pianist’s apartment. He returned two days earlier and has resumed work at his old firm. His reserve disappoints her after her hopes for their reunion.

snapshots.name: Robert Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Madame Lebrun’s elder son
snapshots.body: He admits that loving Edna drove him away to Mexico and brought him back. He imagined her becoming his wife; she insists that she is free to choose, rather than her husband’s to give away.

snapshots.name: Robert Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Madame Lebrun’s elder son
snapshots.body: While Edna was away with Adèle, he left the pigeon house. His note says that he is saying goodbye because he loves her.

introduction.name: Robert Lebrun
introduction.subtitle: Madame Lebrun’s elder son
introduction.body: Robert is the elder son of the woman who runs the Grand Isle holiday cottages. He works in New Orleans and spends his summers here with his family.

snapshots.name: Adèle Ratignolle
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s friend; Alphonse Ratignolle’s wife
snapshots.body: The graceful woman who brings her sewing to sit with Edna. Devotion to her husband and children shapes her life.

snapshots.name: Adèle Ratignolle
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s friend; Alphonse Ratignolle’s wife
snapshots.body: The affectionate friend whose openness contrasts with Edna’s reserve. During their morning at the beach, she listened as Edna shared memories and rested her head on her shoulder.

snapshots.name: Adèle Ratignolle
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s friend; Alphonse Ratignolle’s wife
snapshots.body: She has privately warned Robert that Edna might take his attentions seriously. She regards harmless flirtation as compatible with married life, but taking it further as a breach of trust.

snapshots.name: Adèle Ratignolle
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s friend; Alphonse Ratignolle’s wife
snapshots.body: Back in New Orleans, she lives with her family above her husband’s drugstore. She encourages Edna’s painting and shares an affectionate, closely united household with her husband.

snapshots.name: Adèle Ratignolle
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s friend; Alphonse Ratignolle’s wife
snapshots.body: She has visited the pigeon house, asked Edna to stay with her when she gives birth, and warned that Arobin’s frequent visits may harm Edna’s reputation.

snapshots.name: Adèle Ratignolle
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s friend; Alphonse Ratignolle’s wife
snapshots.body: Edna has kept her company through a painful labor. Exhausted afterward, she urged Edna to think of her children.

introduction.name: Adèle Ratignolle
introduction.subtitle: Edna’s friend; Alphonse Ratignolle’s wife
introduction.body: Adèle is Edna’s affectionate friend at Grand Isle. She is married to Alphonse Ratignolle, a pharmacist, and is devoted to her husband and children.

snapshots.name: Mademoiselle Reisz
snapshots.subtitle: A talented, outspoken pianist
snapshots.body: The small, outspoken pianist with artificial violets in her hair. She has quarreled with many of the holiday guests but has agreed to play at Edna’s request.

snapshots.name: Mademoiselle Reisz
snapshots.subtitle: A talented, outspoken pianist
snapshots.body: Her playing stirred feelings in Edna so strongly that she trembled and cried. The pianist noticed her response and singled her out as a listener worth playing for.

snapshots.name: Mademoiselle Reisz
snapshots.subtitle: A talented, outspoken pianist
snapshots.body: The outspoken musician whose playing moved Edna at Grand Isle. She likes Robert, speaks harshly of his family, and has given Edna her address in the city.

snapshots.name: Mademoiselle Reisz
snapshots.subtitle: A talented, outspoken pianist
snapshots.body: Edna has found her in a small apartment dominated by her piano. She has let Edna read a letter from Robert and told her that an artist needs a courageous soul.

snapshots.name: Mademoiselle Reisz
snapshots.subtitle: A talented, outspoken pianist
snapshots.body: She shares Robert’s letters with Edna and believes that he loves her. Edna has now admitted her own love for him. Her music continues to offer Edna relief and freedom.

introduction.name: Mademoiselle Reisz
introduction.subtitle: A talented, outspoken pianist
introduction.body: Mademoiselle Reisz is an unmarried pianist among the Grand Isle guests. Her blunt manner makes her difficult company, but her music commands attention.

snapshots.name: Alcée Arobin
snapshots.subtitle: A man in New Orleans society
snapshots.body: Robert brings him up while telling Adèle a story involving a consul’s wife at Biloxi. The reference comes as Robert deflects her warning about his own attentions to Edna.

snapshots.name: Alcée Arobin
snapshots.subtitle: A man in New Orleans society
snapshots.body: He was at the races with women who joined Edna and her father. After dinner, Doctor Mandelet privately worries that Arobin might be involved in Edna’s changed behavior.

snapshots.name: Alcée Arobin
snapshots.subtitle: A man in New Orleans society
snapshots.body: The easy-mannered acquaintance from the races. He admires Edna and has arranged through Mrs. Highcamp, their fellow racegoer, to spend another afternoon with her.

snapshots.name: Alcée Arobin
snapshots.subtitle: A man in New Orleans society
snapshots.body: After an afternoon at the races, he stayed to dinner and kissed Edna’s hand. She asked him to leave, but his manner and touch stirred her physically.

snapshots.name: Alcée Arobin
snapshots.subtitle: A man in New Orleans society
snapshots.body: His visits have grown frequent and intimate. Edna has responded to his kiss with desire, while recognizing that her love is for Robert.

snapshots.name: Alcée Arobin
snapshots.subtitle: A man in New Orleans society
snapshots.body: He helped with her move, attended her farewell dinner, and sent flowers to the pigeon house. After the party he accompanied her there and stayed, continuing his caresses.

introduction.name: Arobin
introduction.subtitle: A man in New Orleans society
introduction.body: Alcée Arobin belongs to the fashionable social world around the New Orleans characters. His name first comes up in Robert’s gossip.

snapshots.name: Madame Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Proprietor of the Grand Isle holiday cottages
snapshots.body: Madame Lebrun owns and runs the Grand Isle summer boarding house and cottages where the Pontelliers are staying. She is directing the servants as the guests relax.

snapshots.name: Madame Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Proprietor of the Grand Isle holiday cottages
snapshots.body: She runs the main house and holiday cottages where the Pontelliers are staying. Robert, the young man spending time with Edna, is her son.

snapshots.name: Madame Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Proprietor of the Grand Isle holiday cottages
snapshots.body: The woman who runs the Grand Isle cottages. Robert and the headstrong younger Victor are her sons. Her husband died early in their marriage; Montel has long hoped to take his place.

snapshots.name: Madame Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Proprietor of the Grand Isle holiday cottages
snapshots.body: The mother of Robert and Victor. The pianist calls her Aline and claims that she favors Victor, while Robert contributes much of his earnings to the family.

snapshots.name: Madame Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Proprietor of the Grand Isle holiday cottages
snapshots.body: Edna has visited her New Orleans home to hear news of Robert in Mexico. She also supplied the pianist’s current address.

introduction.name: Madame Lebrun
introduction.subtitle: Proprietor of the Grand Isle holiday cottages
introduction.body: Madame Lebrun owns and runs the summer boarding house and cottages at Grand Isle, where the Pontelliers are staying. Robert and Victor are her sons.

snapshots.name: Victor Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Robert’s younger brother; Madame Lebrun’s son
snapshots.body: The young man who drove away despite his mother’s calls. He is the younger son of the woman who runs the holiday cottages, with a stubborn will and quick temper.

snapshots.name: Victor Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Robert’s younger brother; Madame Lebrun’s son
snapshots.body: He keeps the island property in order during winter and comes to the city for amusement. He has welcomed Edna at his mother’s house and entertained her with tales of his evening out.

snapshots.name: Victor Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Robert’s younger brother; Madame Lebrun’s son
snapshots.body: At Edna’s farewell dinner, Mrs. Highcamp dressed him in roses and a scarf. When he began a song associated with Robert, Edna stopped him abruptly.

snapshots.name: Victor Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Robert’s younger brother; Madame Lebrun’s son
snapshots.body: Back at Grand Isle, he has been repairing the galleries and telling Mariequita about Edna’s dinner. Edna’s unexpected arrival has sent him hurrying to arrange a room and food.

introduction.name: Victor
introduction.subtitle: Robert’s younger brother; Madame Lebrun’s son
introduction.body: Victor is Madame Lebrun’s younger son and Robert’s brother. He belongs to the family that runs the Grand Isle holiday cottages.

snapshots.name: Raoul
snapshots.subtitle: Edna and Léonce’s older son
snapshots.body: The child whose father says he has a fever. Edna is sure he went to bed well and disagrees that he is ill.

snapshots.name: Raoul
snapshots.subtitle: Edna and Léonce’s older son
snapshots.body: One of Edna’s two sons. Unlike his younger brother Etienne, who resisted bedtime, he was already asleep when their mother returned from her day across the bay.

snapshots.name: Raoul
snapshots.subtitle: Edna and Léonce’s older son
snapshots.body: He is with his brother at their grandmother’s country home. His cheerful letter asks for sweets and tells Edna about a litter of tiny white pigs.

introduction.name: Raoul
introduction.subtitle: Edna and Léonce’s older son
introduction.body: Raoul is the older of the Pontelliers’ two young boys. His younger brother is Etienne.

snapshots.name: Etienne
snapshots.subtitle: Edna and Léonce’s younger son
snapshots.body: The little boy who would not go to bed while his mother was away. Adèle brought him back, and Edna is soothing him in her arms.

snapshots.name: Etienne
snapshots.subtitle: Edna and Léonce’s younger son
snapshots.body: He and his brother are staying with their grandmother in Iberville. During Edna’s visit, the boys eagerly told her about the animals, fishing, and games there.

introduction.name: Etienne
introduction.subtitle: Edna and Léonce’s younger son
introduction.body: Etienne is the younger of the Pontelliers’ two boys. His older brother is Raoul.

snapshots.name: The Pontellier boys
snapshots.subtitle: Raoul and Etienne, Edna and Léonce’s sons
snapshots.body: Mr. Pontellier’s two small sons, playing among the other children at the holiday cottages.

snapshots.name: The Pontellier boys
snapshots.subtitle: Raoul and Etienne, Edna and Léonce’s sons
snapshots.body: Edna’s two sons. Raoul is the older; Etienne is the younger boy she has just soothed after his difficult bedtime.

introduction.name: The Pontellier boys
introduction.subtitle: Raoul and Etienne, Edna and Léonce’s sons
introduction.body: The Pontelliers’ two young sons are Raoul and Etienne. They are staying at Grand Isle with their parents and their nurse.

snapshots.name: The Farival twins
snapshots.subtitle: Monsieur Farival’s piano-playing granddaughters
snapshots.body: The girls playing a piano duet while the holiday house bustles around Mr. Pontellier.

snapshots.name: The Farival twins
snapshots.subtitle: Monsieur Farival’s piano-playing granddaughters
snapshots.body: The girls who play familiar duets for the holiday guests. They dress in blue and white. The elderly Monsieur Farival, annoyed by the parrot’s interruption, is their grandfather.

introduction.name: The Farival twins
introduction.subtitle: Monsieur Farival’s piano-playing granddaughters
introduction.body: The Farival twins are fourteen-year-old girls among the holiday guests. They play piano duets; Monsieur Farival is their grandfather.

snapshots.name: Monsieur Farival
snapshots.subtitle: The Farival twins’ grandfather
snapshots.body: The older man to whom Adèle openly recounted a childbirth, surprising Edna with her frankness.

snapshots.name: Monsieur Farival
snapshots.subtitle: The Farival twins’ grandfather
snapshots.body: The elderly man who objected to the parrot interrupting his granddaughters’ piano performance. The girls are the familiar duet-playing twins.

snapshots.name: Monsieur Farival
snapshots.subtitle: The Farival twins’ grandfather
snapshots.body: The piano-playing twins’ grandfather. On the boat to church he keeps offering opinions about sailing, irritating Beaudelet, the boatman.

introduction.name: Monsieur Farival
introduction.subtitle: The Farival twins’ grandfather
introduction.body: Monsieur Farival is an elderly guest at Grand Isle and the grandfather of the two girls who play piano duets.

snapshots.name: The lady in black
snapshots.subtitle: An unnamed, devout holiday guest
snapshots.body: The woman walking quietly near the cottages, counting her prayer beads.

snapshots.name: The lady in black
snapshots.subtitle: An unnamed, devout holiday guest
snapshots.body: The woman often seen reading prayers or counting her beads. She has joined the boat trip to church, keeping apart from the lovers and the talkative passengers.

introduction.name: The lady in black
introduction.subtitle: An unnamed, devout holiday guest
introduction.body: A woman among the Grand Isle guests, recognizable by her black clothes and prayer beads. The novel does not give her a personal name.

snapshots.name: The young lovers
snapshots.subtitle: An unnamed young couple at Grand Isle
snapshots.body: The couple exchanging endearments beneath the children’s tent at the beach.

snapshots.name: The young lovers
snapshots.subtitle: An unnamed young couple at Grand Isle
snapshots.body: The couple who keep apart from the holiday company, intent on each other. They have joined the church excursion; Robert tells Mariequita that they are not married.

introduction.name: The young lovers
introduction.subtitle: An unnamed young couple at Grand Isle
introduction.body: The young lovers are two holiday guests who keep close together, absorbed in each other. They are not given personal names.

snapshots.name: The children’s nurse
snapshots.subtitle: The Pontellier boys’ nurse
snapshots.body: The nurse following Mr. Pontellier’s two boys while they play. The text identifies her by a racial description rather than a personal name.

snapshots.name: The children’s nurse
snapshots.subtitle: The Pontellier boys’ nurse
snapshots.body: The woman who cares for Edna’s children. She has gone with the boys to their grandmother’s country home while their father is away.

introduction.name: The children’s nurse
introduction.subtitle: The Pontellier boys’ nurse
introduction.body: The woman employed to look after Edna and Léonce’s sons, Raoul and Etienne. The narrator identifies her by a racial description rather than a personal name.

snapshots.name: Edna’s father
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s father; a former army colonel
snapshots.body: Edna mentions his Mississippi plantation while talking about her earlier life.

snapshots.name: Edna’s father
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s father; a former army colonel
snapshots.body: Edna remembers the gloom of his Sunday prayers. He and her older sister opposed her marriage to a Catholic.

snapshots.name: Edna’s father
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s father; a former army colonel
snapshots.body: Edna’s father, a former Confederate colonel, has come to buy wedding presents and clothes. He sits stiffly for her sketch and takes her talent seriously.

snapshots.name: Edna’s father
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s father; a former army colonel
snapshots.body: He has argued with Edna over her refusal to attend her sister’s wedding. Before leaving, he advises her husband to manage her through authority and coercion.

introduction.name: Edna’s father
introduction.subtitle: Edna’s father; a former army colonel
introduction.body: Edna’s father is a former colonel associated with her childhood plantation home. He is also the father of her sisters, Margaret and Janet.

snapshots.name: Edna’s mother
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s deceased mother
snapshots.body: She died when Edna and her sisters were young. Margaret, the older sister, took on responsibilities in the household.

snapshots.name: Edna’s mother
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s deceased mother
snapshots.body: Edna’s mother died during her childhood. Money from her estate now forms part of the income Edna plans to use for a home of her own.

introduction.name: Edna’s mother
introduction.subtitle: Edna’s deceased mother
introduction.body: Edna’s mother died when her daughters were young. Margaret, the oldest sister, took on responsibilities in the household.

snapshots.name: Janet
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s younger sister
snapshots.body: Edna has been discussing a wedding present for her sister.

snapshots.name: Janet
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s younger sister
snapshots.body: The sister whose wedding is approaching. Edna remembers that they often quarreled when they were younger.

snapshots.name: Janet
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s younger sister
snapshots.body: Edna has refused to attend her wedding despite a heated argument with their father. Léonce plans to attend on his way to New York.

introduction.name: Janet
introduction.subtitle: Edna’s younger sister
introduction.body: Janet is Edna’s younger sister. Her approaching wedding is a subject of family conversation.

snapshots.name: Margaret
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s older sister
snapshots.body: She assumed household responsibilities after their mother died. Edna remembers her as dignified and reserved rather than openly affectionate.

snapshots.name: Margaret
snapshots.subtitle: Edna’s older sister
snapshots.body: Edna’s practical older sister, who helped fill their mother’s place. She and their father strongly opposed Edna’s marriage to a Catholic.

introduction.name: Margaret
introduction.subtitle: Edna’s older sister
introduction.body: Margaret is Edna’s older sister. After their mother died, she took on some of the responsibilities of a mother in the family.

snapshots.name: Madame Pontellier, the boys’ grandmother
snapshots.subtitle: Léonce’s mother; the boys’ grandmother
snapshots.body: Edna’s boys have stayed with their grandmother in the country before. Edna felt reassured that they were happy and well cared for there.

snapshots.name: Madame Pontellier, the boys’ grandmother
snapshots.subtitle: Léonce’s mother; the boys’ grandmother
snapshots.body: She has taken the boys and their nurse to Iberville. Deeply attached to her grandchildren, she wants them to enjoy the country life their father knew as a child.

introduction.name: Grandmother Pontellier
introduction.subtitle: Léonce’s mother; the boys’ grandmother
introduction.body: Old Madame Pontellier is Léonce’s mother and the grandmother of Raoul and Etienne. Her home is in Iberville.

snapshots.name: Alphonse Ratignolle
snapshots.subtitle: Adèle’s husband; a New Orleans pharmacist
snapshots.body: The husband Adèle jokes might be jealous of Robert. Their teasing treats Robert’s earlier devotion to her as harmless.

snapshots.name: Alphonse Ratignolle
snapshots.subtitle: Adèle’s husband; a New Orleans pharmacist
snapshots.body: Adèle’s husband runs the drugstore beneath their New Orleans home. Cheerful and hospitable, he shares an affectionate household with the friend who encourages Edna’s painting.

snapshots.name: Alphonse Ratignolle
snapshots.subtitle: Adèle’s husband; a New Orleans pharmacist
snapshots.body: The drugstore owner is grateful that Edna has come to comfort his wife during childbirth. Her sister could not come, and Adèle wanted Edna beside her.

introduction.name: Monsieur Ratignolle
introduction.subtitle: Adèle’s husband; a New Orleans pharmacist
introduction.body: Alphonse Ratignolle is Adèle’s husband. He runs a drugstore in New Orleans, where the family lives above the shop.

snapshots.name: Mademoiselle Duvigne
snapshots.subtitle: A former summer companion of Robert
snapshots.body: Robert devoted two summers to her before she died. Her name comes up as the narrator describes his habit of attending a woman each season.

introduction.name: Mademoiselle Duvigne
introduction.subtitle: A former summer companion of Robert
introduction.body: Madame Duvigné is a woman Robert used to spend time with during an earlier summer at Grand Isle.

snapshots.name: Beaudelet
snapshots.subtitle: The boatman at Grand Isle
snapshots.body: Some of the holiday guests have crossed to the Chênière in his lugger to attend mass.

snapshots.name: Beaudelet
snapshots.subtitle: The boatman at Grand Isle
snapshots.body: He is sailing the party to church. Monsieur Farival’s opinions about handling the boat annoy him, but he directs his complaints at Mariequita instead.

snapshots.name: Beaudelet
snapshots.subtitle: The boatman at Grand Isle
snapshots.body: His night voyage carrying vegetables gave Robert a way to reach New Orleans for the onward trip to Mexico. Edna heard his voice as the two men left.

introduction.name: Beaudelet
introduction.subtitle: The boatman at Grand Isle
introduction.body: Beaudelet handles the boat that carries people between Grand Isle and Chênière Caminada, across the bay.

snapshots.name: Mariequita
snapshots.subtitle: A young island woman who knows the Lebruns
snapshots.body: The young Spanish-speaking passenger on the boat to church. Robert knows her and talks with her; she appeals to him when the boatman complains about her.

snapshots.name: Mariequita
snapshots.subtitle: A young island woman who knows the Lebruns
snapshots.body: The barefoot girl who carried shrimps across the bay. The pianist says Robert once fought Victor over his behavior toward her; Edna dislikes the bitterness of the account.

snapshots.name: Mariequita
snapshots.subtitle: A young island woman who knows the Lebruns
snapshots.body: She has been handing Victor nails as he repairs the galleries and listening to his account of Edna’s dinner. When Edna arrives unexpectedly, she brings towels and is sent to find a cook.

introduction.name: Mariequita
introduction.subtitle: A young island woman who knows the Lebruns
introduction.body: Mariequita is a young Spanish-speaking woman from the island community. She knows Robert and Victor Lebrun.

snapshots.name: Madame Antoine
snapshots.subtitle: A hospitable woman on Chênière Caminada
snapshots.body: Robert has brought Edna to her clean little home after she felt faint in church. She welcomes them warmly and helps Edna settle comfortably.

snapshots.name: Madame Antoine
snapshots.subtitle: A hospitable woman on Chênière Caminada
snapshots.body: The woman who gave Edna a bed and food after church. She and her son Tonie live on the Chênière; her evening tales of the islands and sea held Edna and Robert there until night.

introduction.name: Madame Antoine
introduction.subtitle: A hospitable woman on Chênière Caminada
introduction.body: Madame Antoine lives on the island across the bay from Grand Isle. Tonie is her son.

snapshots.name: Tonie
snapshots.subtitle: Madame Antoine’s son
snapshots.body: Robert proposes asking him to patch and trim a boat for outings with Edna.

snapshots.name: Tonie
snapshots.subtitle: Madame Antoine’s son
snapshots.body: The son of the woman who gave Edna a place to rest after church. He talked with Robert while she slept, and his boat will carry them back to Grand Isle.

introduction.name: Tonie
introduction.subtitle: Madame Antoine’s son
introduction.body: Tonie is the son of Madame Antoine, who lives on Chênière Caminada. He helps with boats and crossings between the islands.

snapshots.name: Monsieur Lebrun
snapshots.subtitle: Madame Lebrun’s deceased husband
snapshots.body: The father of Robert and Victor died early in their parents’ marriage. Their mother often imagines that things would have gone better had he lived.

introduction.name: Monsieur Lebrun
introduction.subtitle: Madame Lebrun’s deceased husband
introduction.body: Monsieur Lebrun was Madame Lebrun’s husband and the father of Robert and Victor. He died early in the marriage.

snapshots.name: Montel
snapshots.subtitle: Madame Lebrun’s longstanding admirer
snapshots.body: The middle-aged man who has long hoped to take the late Monsieur Lebrun’s place in the family. He has sent word that Robert might join him in Vera Cruz.

snapshots.name: Montel
snapshots.subtitle: Madame Lebrun’s longstanding admirer
snapshots.body: The longtime admirer of Robert’s mother. Robert has met him in Mexico and reports that he is helping him get ahead, though his income has not yet improved.

introduction.name: Montel
introduction.subtitle: Madame Lebrun’s longstanding admirer
introduction.body: Montel is a man in Mexico who has long been interested in the widowed Madame Lebrun. He is an acquaintance of her family.

snapshots.name: Francisco
snapshots.subtitle: A man mentioned in Mariequita’s island gossip
snapshots.body: Mariequita says he ran away with a married woman, taking her husband’s money, a child, and his boat.

introduction.name: Francisco
introduction.subtitle: A man mentioned in Mariequita’s island gossip
introduction.body: Francisco belongs to the local story Mariequita tells Robert. He does not appear as a participant in the main action.

snapshots.name: Sylvano
snapshots.subtitle: A married man in Mariequita’s island gossip
snapshots.body: According to Mariequita, his wife ran away with Francisco. The pair took his money, one of the children, and his boat.

introduction.name: Sylvano
introduction.subtitle: A married man in Mariequita’s island gossip
introduction.body: Sylvano is a man whose wife is the subject of Mariequita’s story to Robert.

snapshots.name: Sylvano’s wife
snapshots.subtitle: Sylvano’s wife
snapshots.body: Mariequita says this mother of four ran away with Francisco, taking a child, money, and her husband’s boat.

introduction.name: Sylvano’s wife
introduction.subtitle: Sylvano’s wife
introduction.body: An unnamed woman in Mariequita’s account of life in the island community. She is married to Sylvano and has children.

snapshots.name: Father Fochel
snapshots.subtitle: A priest at the cathedral
snapshots.body: The cathedral priest tried to explain whether the indulgence attached to the lady in black’s Mexican prayer beads applied elsewhere. His explanation did not satisfy her.

introduction.name: Father Fochel
introduction.subtitle: A priest at the cathedral
introduction.body: Father Fochel is the cathedral priest mentioned in connection with prayer beads and an indulgence.

snapshots.name: The consul’s wife at Biloxi
snapshots.subtitle: An unnamed consul’s wife at Biloxi
snapshots.body: Robert mentions her in a story involving Alcée Arobin while turning the conversation away from Adèle’s warning about Edna.

introduction.name: The consul’s wife
introduction.subtitle: An unnamed consul’s wife at Biloxi
introduction.body: The wife of a consul, mentioned in Robert’s gossip about Alcée Arobin. The novel does not give her a personal name.

aliases: the tenor of the French Opera
the tenor at the French Opera

snapshots.name: The French Opera tenor
snapshots.subtitle: An unnamed French Opera singer
snapshots.body: Robert tells a story about this singer receiving letters that should not have been written. It is one of the anecdotes with which he changes the subject.

introduction.name: The French Opera tenor
introduction.subtitle: An unnamed French Opera singer
introduction.body: A tenor associated with the French Opera in New Orleans. Robert mentions him in a story he tells Adèle.

snapshots.name: Joe
snapshots.subtitle: A servant in the Pontelliers’ household
snapshots.body: The boy serving at the Pontelliers’ New Orleans home. Edna instructed him to tell callers she was out; he now brings the tray of their cards to her husband.

snapshots.name: Joe
snapshots.subtitle: A servant in the Pontelliers’ household
snapshots.body: The boy who served meals and admitted callers at the family house. He is now working at the small house Edna plans to move into.

introduction.name: Joe
introduction.subtitle: A servant in the Pontelliers’ household
introduction.body: Joe works for Edna and Léonce at their New Orleans home.

snapshots.name: Mrs. Belthrop
snapshots.subtitle: A social acquaintance of the Pontelliers
snapshots.body: One of the women whose visit Edna missed. Her husband’s business is valuable to Léonce, who urges Edna to send her a note.

introduction.name: Mrs. Belthrop
introduction.subtitle: A social acquaintance of the Pontelliers
introduction.body: Mrs. Belthrop belongs to the Pontelliers’ New Orleans visiting circle. Her husband is an important business connection of Léonce’s.

snapshots.name: Mr. Belthrop
snapshots.subtitle: A business connection of Léonce’s
snapshots.body: Léonce says his business is worth a great deal to him. This is why he is particularly concerned that Edna missed Mrs. Belthrop’s visit.

introduction.name: Mr. Belthrop
introduction.subtitle: A business connection of Léonce’s
introduction.body: Mr. Belthrop is the husband of Mrs. Belthrop, one of the Pontelliers’ social acquaintances. Léonce values his business.

snapshots.name: The Misses Delasidas
snapshots.subtitle: Daughters of one of Léonce’s business connections
snapshots.body: Their visiting card is among those Edna left unanswered. Léonce says he completed a large futures transaction for their father that morning.

introduction.name: The Misses Delasidas
introduction.subtitle: Daughters of one of Léonce’s business connections
introduction.body: The Misses Delasidas belong to the Pontelliers’ visiting circle. Their father does business with Léonce.

snapshots.name: Mrs. Highcamp
snapshots.subtitle: A married woman in Edna’s social circle
snapshots.body: Her card is among those left while Edna was out. Léonce says he would prefer Edna to see less of her.

snapshots.name: Mrs. Highcamp
snapshots.subtitle: A married woman in Edna’s social circle
snapshots.body: The tall, composed woman who goes to the races with Edna and Arobin. She cultivates fashionable young men through her daughter’s social circle and has invited Edna to dine with her family.

snapshots.name: Mrs. Highcamp
snapshots.subtitle: A married woman in Edna’s social circle
snapshots.body: At Edna’s farewell dinner, she devoted much of her attention to the hostess’s young acquaintance Victor. She draped him in roses and a scarf, then invited him to visit her daughter.

introduction.name: Mrs. Highcamp
introduction.subtitle: A married woman in Edna’s social circle
introduction.body: Mrs. Highcamp is a worldly New Orleans acquaintance with a grown daughter. She enjoys society and outings to the races.

snapshots.name: Mr. Highcamp
snapshots.subtitle: Mrs. Highcamp’s husband
snapshots.body: The bald, unresponsive man at the dinner following the races. His wife addresses him with careful courtesy; afterward, they sit together reading newspapers.

introduction.name: Mr. Highcamp
introduction.subtitle: Mrs. Highcamp’s husband
introduction.body: Mr. Highcamp is the husband of Mrs. Highcamp and the father of their grown daughter.

snapshots.name: Miss Highcamp
snapshots.subtitle: Mr. and Mrs. Highcamp’s daughter
snapshots.body: The young woman who chose a Dante reading over the races. After dinner at her family’s home, she plays Grieg while Edna listens.

introduction.name: Miss Highcamp
introduction.subtitle: Mr. and Mrs. Highcamp’s daughter
introduction.body: Miss Highcamp is the Highcamps’ grown daughter. Her interests include music and literary readings.

snapshots.name: Madame Laforcé
snapshots.subtitle: A visitor from Carrolton
snapshots.body: One of the women whose visiting cards Léonce reads aloud. He remarks that she came all the way from Carrolton while Edna was out.

introduction.name: Madame Laforcé
introduction.subtitle: A visitor from Carrolton
introduction.body: Mrs. Laforcé is an acquaintance in the Pontelliers’ visiting circle. She comes from Carrolton.

snapshots.name: Miss Wiggs
snapshots.subtitle: A social acquaintance of the Pontelliers
snapshots.body: Her name appears on a visiting card Léonce reads aloud during their disagreement about Edna’s reception afternoon.

introduction.name: Miss Wiggs
introduction.subtitle: A social acquaintance of the Pontelliers
introduction.body: Mrs. Wiggs is one of the women who call at the Pontelliers’ New Orleans home.

snapshots.name: Mrs. Eleanor Boltons
snapshots.subtitle: A social acquaintance of the Pontelliers
snapshots.body: Her visiting card is among those Léonce reads while arguing that Edna should have observed her usual reception day.

introduction.name: Mrs. Eleanor Boltons
introduction.subtitle: A social acquaintance of the Pontelliers
introduction.body: Miss Eleanor Boltons is one of the callers in the Pontelliers’ New Orleans social circle.

snapshots.name: ’Cité
snapshots.subtitle: A servant in the Ratignolle household
snapshots.body: The young woman Adèle calls to sort the returned washing. She is asked to check a missing handkerchief and set aside anything needing repair.

introduction.name: ’Cité
introduction.subtitle: A servant in the Ratignolle household
introduction.body: ’Cité works for Adèle and Alphonse Ratignolle. She is mentioned in connection with the household laundry.

snapshots.name: Laidpore
snapshots.subtitle: An artist and possible teacher for Edna
snapshots.body: Edna mentions him while discussing whether to return to painting and develop her skills.

snapshots.name: Laidpore
snapshots.subtitle: An artist and possible teacher for Edna
snapshots.body: He praises the growing strength and individuality of her work. Edna has sold sketches through him, helping make her plan for a separate home possible.

introduction.name: Laidpore
introduction.subtitle: An artist and possible teacher for Edna
introduction.body: Laidpore is an artist whose name comes up as a possible painting teacher for Edna.

snapshots.name: Madame Pouponne
snapshots.subtitle: A resident at Mademoiselle Reisz’s former address
snapshots.body: The woman Edna meets while searching for Mademoiselle Reisz. Her family now occupies the house and rents furnished rooms, but knows nothing of the pianist’s whereabouts.

introduction.name: Madame Pouponne
introduction.subtitle: A resident at Mademoiselle Reisz’s former address
introduction.body: Madame Pouponne occupies rooms at the address where Edna looks for the pianist. She is a different person from Mademoiselle Reisz.

snapshots.name: Doctor Mandelet
snapshots.subtitle: The Pontelliers’ physician and family friend
snapshots.body: The older, partly retired doctor whom Léonce visits. He is a family friend, valued for his judgment and consulted by a small circle of households.

snapshots.name: Doctor Mandelet
snapshots.subtitle: The Pontelliers’ physician and family friend
snapshots.body: Léonce has consulted him about Edna’s changed behavior. He recommends patience and privately wonders whether another man might be involved.

snapshots.name: Doctor Mandelet
snapshots.subtitle: The Pontelliers’ physician and family friend
snapshots.body: At dinner he found Edna animated rather than listless. On his way home he privately worried that Arobin might be involved in the changes her husband described.

snapshots.name: Doctor Mandelet
snapshots.subtitle: The Pontelliers’ physician and family friend
snapshots.body: After attending Adèle’s childbirth, he walked Edna home. Sensing her distress, he invited her to confide in him without pressing her to explain.

introduction.name: Doctor Mandelet
introduction.subtitle: The Pontelliers’ physician and family friend
introduction.body: Doctor Mandelet is an experienced, partly retired physician in New Orleans. He knows the Pontellier family.

snapshots.name: Mrs. Merriman
snapshots.subtitle: A society acquaintance and fellow racegoer
snapshots.body: One of the women who joined Edna and her father at the racecourse, in company with Arobin.

snapshots.name: Mrs. Merriman
snapshots.subtitle: A society acquaintance and fellow racegoer
snapshots.body: The vivacious woman at Edna’s farewell dinner. She interrupts her husband’s rambling anecdote to discuss books with the quiet newspaper man beside her.

snapshots.name: Mrs. Merriman
snapshots.subtitle: A society acquaintance and fellow racegoer
snapshots.body: After attending Edna’s farewell dinner, she invited her to a card party. Arobin has brought word that a child’s illness has postponed it; Edna decides not to attend.

introduction.name: Mrs. Merriman
introduction.subtitle: A society acquaintance and fellow racegoer
introduction.body: Mrs. Merriman belongs to the social circle Edna encounters at the races. Mr. Merriman is her husband.

snapshots.name: Mr. Merriman
snapshots.subtitle: Mrs. Merriman’s husband
snapshots.body: The jovial man who laughs readily at other people’s jokes. When his wife interrupts his story at Edna’s dinner, he tells it privately to Miss Mayblunt instead.

introduction.name: Mr. Merriman
introduction.subtitle: Mrs. Merriman’s husband
introduction.body: Mr. Merriman is a sociable man in the circle around Edna. He is married to Mrs. Merriman, the racegoer.

snapshots.name: Celestine
snapshots.subtitle: A woman who does domestic work for Edna
snapshots.body: The older woman who occasionally works for Edna. She has offered to live with her and manage the work in the small house Edna plans to rent.

snapshots.name: Celestine
snapshots.subtitle: A woman who does domestic work for Edna
snapshots.body: She cooks and looks after Edna’s small home. While serving Robert dinner, she stops to speak with him in patois; she has known him since he was a boy.

introduction.name: Celestine
introduction.subtitle: A woman who does domestic work for Edna
introduction.body: Célestine is an older woman who has worked for Edna from time to time.

snapshots.name: Ellen
snapshots.subtitle: A maid in the Pontellier household
snapshots.body: The woman working beside Edna as she packs and takes down pictures. She coined the name pigeon house for the small home around the corner.

introduction.name: Ellen
introduction.subtitle: A maid in the Pontellier household
introduction.body: Ellen works as a maid at Edna and Léonce’s New Orleans home.

snapshots.name: Miss Mayblunt
snapshots.subtitle: An intellectually inclined social acquaintance
snapshots.body: The observant, intellectually inclined woman at Edna’s dinner. People suspect she writes under a pen name. She has arrived with Gouvernail, a quiet man connected with a newspaper.

introduction.name: Miss Mayblunt
introduction.subtitle: An intellectually inclined social acquaintance
introduction.body: Miss Mayblunt belongs to Edna’s social circle. People suspect that she writes under a pen name, but the narrator does not confirm it.

snapshots.name: Gouvernail
snapshots.subtitle: A newspaper man; Miss Mayblunt’s companion
snapshots.body: The observant guest who came to Edna’s dinner with Miss Mayblunt, the woman with the lorgnettes. He is connected with one of the daily newspapers.

introduction.name: Gouvernail
introduction.subtitle: A newspaper man; Miss Mayblunt’s companion
introduction.body: Gouvernail is a quiet newspaper man in Edna’s social circle. He accompanies Miss Mayblunt.

snapshots.name: Laitner
snapshots.subtitle: A lawyer acquainted with Arobin
snapshots.body: Arobin says this friend lets his name appear on the law firm’s letterhead and sign. The admission follows a question about whether he belongs to the firm.

introduction.name: Laitner
introduction.subtitle: A lawyer acquainted with Arobin
introduction.body: Laitner is a lawyer connected with Alcée Arobin. His name comes up in connection with Arobin’s stationery.

snapshots.name: Uncle Jasper
snapshots.subtitle: The boys’ Uncle Jasper
snapshots.body: Edna’s children tell her about fishing with him in the lake during their stay in Iberville.

introduction.name: Uncle Jasper
introduction.subtitle: The boys’ Uncle Jasper
introduction.body: Uncle Jasper is a relative mentioned by Raoul and Etienne during their country visit. The passage does not specify which side of the family he belongs to.

snapshots.name: Lidie
snapshots.subtitle: The mother of the boys’ country playmates
snapshots.body: Her children pick pecans with Edna’s boys during their stay in Iberville.

snapshots.name: Lidie
snapshots.subtitle: The mother of the boys’ country playmates
snapshots.body: Her children play with Edna’s boys in Iberville. Raoul’s letter reports ten tiny piglets beside her large white pig.

introduction.name: Lidie
introduction.subtitle: The mother of the boys’ country playmates
introduction.body: Lidie is a woman whose children play with Raoul and Etienne in Iberville.

snapshots.name: Susie
snapshots.subtitle: An older woman the boys know in the country
snapshots.body: Edna’s boys delight in hauling real wood chips for her fire during their stay in the country. The text describes her as older and lame.

introduction.name: Susie
introduction.subtitle: An older woman the boys know in the country
introduction.body: Old Susie is a woman Raoul and Etienne mention when describing their time in Iberville.

snapshots.name: Catiche
snapshots.subtitle: The woman who runs a garden café
snapshots.body: The woman running the quiet garden eating place Edna enjoys. Robert knows her coffee too; this is his first visit since returning from Mexico.

introduction.name: Catiche
introduction.subtitle: The woman who runs a garden café
introduction.body: Catiche runs a small eating place with a garden on the outskirts of New Orleans.

snapshots.name: Joséphine
snapshots.subtitle: Adèle’s maternity nurse
snapshots.body: The experienced woman caring for Adèle during labor. She keeps urging courage and patience while waiting for the doctor.

introduction.name: Joséphine
introduction.subtitle: Adèle’s maternity nurse
introduction.body: Joséphine is the nurse attending Adèle Ratignolle during childbirth.

snapshots.name: Célina
snapshots.subtitle: A married woman in the island community
snapshots.body: Mariequita says she could run away to New Orleans with this woman’s husband while teasing Victor about his admiration for Edna.

introduction.name: Célina
introduction.subtitle: A married woman in the island community
introduction.body: Célina is a local woman mentioned by Mariequita. She does not appear directly in the scene.

snapshots.name: Célina’s husband
snapshots.subtitle: Célina’s husband
snapshots.body: Mariequita has suggested running away with him. Victor responds by threatening to beat him when they meet.

introduction.name: Célina’s husband
introduction.subtitle: Célina’s husband
introduction.body: An unnamed man in the island community, referred to through his marriage to Célina.

snapshots.name: Philomel
snapshots.subtitle: A cook at Grand Isle
snapshots.body: Victor mentions her cooking when arranging a meal for Edna’s unexpected visit. He wonders whether her mother could come to help instead.

introduction.name: Philomel
introduction.subtitle: A cook at Grand Isle
introduction.body: Philomel is a cook associated with the holiday cottages. Her mother also cooks.

snapshots.name: Philomel’s mother
snapshots.subtitle: Philomel’s mother; another cook
snapshots.body: Victor and Mariequita discuss bringing her in to cook during Edna’s stay, if she can be persuaded with sufficient pay.

introduction.name: Philomel’s mother
introduction.subtitle: Philomel’s mother; another cook
introduction.body: The mother of Philomel, the Grand Isle cook. She is mentioned as someone who could prepare a meal.

aliases: a dignified and sad-eyed cavalry officer

snapshots.name: The cavalry officer
snapshots.subtitle: An officer from Edna’s childhood memories
snapshots.body: The sad-eyed officer who visited her father in Kentucky. As a child, Edna was fascinated by him and could scarcely take her eyes off his face.

introduction.name: The cavalry officer
introduction.subtitle: An officer from Edna’s childhood memories
introduction.body: An unnamed cavalry officer who visited Edna’s father when she was a child in Kentucky.

snapshots.name: The engaged young man
snapshots.subtitle: A young man from a neighboring plantation
snapshots.body: The young man visiting a neighboring plantation who was engaged to someone else. As a girl, Edna was distressed to realize she meant nothing to him.

introduction.name: The engaged young man
introduction.subtitle: A young man from a neighboring plantation
introduction.body: An unnamed young man Edna remembers from her youth. He was engaged to another woman.

snapshots.name: The tragedian
snapshots.subtitle: An actor Edna admired in her youth
snapshots.body: As a young woman, Edna became infatuated with a famous tragic actor. She kept his photograph on her desk and concealed the intensity of her feelings.

introduction.name: The tragedian
introduction.subtitle: An actor Edna admired in her youth
introduction.body: An unnamed actor who played tragic roles. He belongs to Edna’s memories of youthful romantic attachments.

aliases: Her most intimate friend at school

snapshots.name: Edna’s school friend
snapshots.subtitle: A friend from Edna’s school years
snapshots.body: The intellectually gifted school friend whose essays Edna admired. They discussed English classics, religion, and politics together.

introduction.name: Edna’s school friend
introduction.subtitle: A friend from Edna’s school years
introduction.body: An unnamed girl with whom Edna shared books and conversation. Edna remembers her as intellectually gifted.

entities.editorialName: The girl working the sewing machine

snapshots.name: The girl working the sewing machine
snapshots.subtitle: A young servant in Madame Lebrun’s household
snapshots.body: The girl seated on the floor working the treadle of Madame Lebrun’s sewing machine by hand.

snapshots.name: The girl working the sewing machine
snapshots.subtitle: A young servant in Madame Lebrun’s household
snapshots.body: The young servant who worked the hostess’s sewing machine. While sweeping the galleries, she is sent to tell Robert that Edna wants him to join the church excursion.

introduction.name: The girl working the sewing machine
introduction.subtitle: A young servant in Madame Lebrun’s household
introduction.body: An unnamed young Black girl who works for Madame Lebrun, helping operate her sewing machine and carrying messages.

snapshots.name: Daudet
snapshots.subtitle: An author Robert reads aloud
snapshots.body: Daudet is the author of the story Robert reads to Edna. He is a literary reference, not a member of the holiday party.

introduction.name: Daudet
introduction.subtitle: An author Robert reads aloud
introduction.body: Daudet is the author of the story Robert reads to Edna. He is a literary reference, not a member of the holiday party.

snapshots.name: Napoleon
snapshots.subtitle: The historical figure used in a comparison
snapshots.body: Napoleon is invoked to describe the appearance of an officer Edna remembers. He is not a character in the action.

introduction.name: Napoleon
introduction.subtitle: The historical figure used in a comparison
introduction.body: Napoleon is invoked to describe the appearance of an officer Edna remembers. He is not a character in the action.

snapshots.name: Goncourt
snapshots.subtitle: A literary name on a borrowed book
snapshots.body: Goncourt is the author’s name given for a book Madame Lebrun lends Edna through Robert. The passage does not identify the title.

introduction.name: Goncourt
introduction.subtitle: A literary name on a borrowed book
introduction.body: Goncourt is the author’s name given for a book Madame Lebrun lends Edna through Robert. The passage does not identify the title.

snapshots.name: Chopin
snapshots.subtitle: A composer whose music Reisz plays
snapshots.body: Chopin is a composer represented in Mademoiselle Reisz’s piano repertoire. This is a musical reference, not a reference to the novel’s author, Kate Chopin.

snapshots.name: Chopin
snapshots.subtitle: A composer whose music Reisz plays
snapshots.body: His impromptu is Robert’s favorite, and Robert has asked the pianist to play it for Edna. She hears it while reading his letter.

introduction.name: Chopin
introduction.subtitle: A composer whose music Reisz plays
introduction.body: Chopin is a composer represented in Mademoiselle Reisz’s piano repertoire. This is a musical reference, not a reference to the novel’s author, Kate Chopin.

snapshots.name: Isolde
snapshots.subtitle: The heroine of Wagner’s Tristan und Isolde
snapshots.body: Isolde is the Irish princess in Wagner’s opera Tristan und Isolde. Mademoiselle Reisz plays music evoking her love.

introduction.name: Isolde
introduction.subtitle: The heroine of Wagner’s Tristan und Isolde
introduction.body: Isolde is the Irish princess in Wagner’s opera Tristan und Isolde. Mademoiselle Reisz plays music evoking her love.

snapshots.name: Emerson
snapshots.subtitle: An American essayist and poet
snapshots.body: Ralph Waldo Emerson is an American essayist and poet. Edna takes up his work as she returns to reading.

introduction.name: Emerson
introduction.subtitle: An American essayist and poet
introduction.body: Ralph Waldo Emerson is an American essayist and poet. Edna takes up his work as she returns to reading.

snapshots.name: Dante
snapshots.subtitle: An author discussed at a literary reading
snapshots.body: Dante is the author whose work features at a reading attended by Miss Highcamp.

introduction.name: Dante
introduction.subtitle: An author discussed at a literary reading
introduction.body: Dante is the author whose work features at a reading attended by Miss Highcamp.

snapshots.name: Grieg
snapshots.subtitle: A composer in Miss Highcamp’s repertoire
snapshots.body: Grieg is the composer of music Miss Highcamp plays on the piano.

introduction.name: Grieg
introduction.subtitle: A composer in Miss Highcamp’s repertoire
introduction.body: Grieg is the composer of music Miss Highcamp plays on the piano.

snapshots.name: Beethoven
snapshots.subtitle: The composer represented by a bust
snapshots.body: Beethoven is a composer. A bust of him stands in Mademoiselle Reisz’s apartment.

introduction.name: Beethoven
introduction.subtitle: The composer represented by a bust
introduction.body: Beethoven is a composer. A bust of him stands in Mademoiselle Reisz’s apartment.

snapshots.name: Venus
snapshots.subtitle: A mythological figure associated with the sea
snapshots.body: Venus is the figure rising from the sea in Victor’s comparison of Edna’s beauty. She is a mythological reference.

introduction.name: Venus
introduction.subtitle: A mythological figure associated with the sea
introduction.body: Venus is the figure rising from the sea in Victor’s comparison of Edna’s beauty. She is a mythological reference.

snapshots.name: The Virgin Mary
snapshots.subtitle: Mary, the mother of Jesus
snapshots.body: The Virgin Mary is a Christian sacred figure. A Madonna is an image of her; the novel uses such images in comparisons of women’s beauty.

snapshots.name: The Virgin Mary
snapshots.subtitle: Mary, the mother of Jesus
snapshots.body: The twins were dedicated to the Blessed Virgin at baptism and dress in her colors, blue and white. Earlier, Edna compared Adèle’s beauty to a Madonna.

introduction.name: The Madonna
introduction.subtitle: Mary, the mother of Jesus
introduction.body: The Virgin Mary is a Christian sacred figure. A Madonna is an image of her; the novel uses such images in comparisons of women’s beauty.

snapshots.name: The Holy Ghost
snapshots.subtitle: The Holy Spirit in Christian belief
snapshots.body: The Holy Ghost is another name for the Holy Spirit. The narrator invokes this religious figure in an aside.

introduction.name: The Holy Ghost
introduction.subtitle: The Holy Spirit in Christian belief
introduction.body: The Holy Ghost is another name for the Holy Spirit. The narrator invokes this religious figure in an aside.

snapshots.name: Gluglu
snapshots.subtitle: An unexplained name in the boys’ country stories
snapshots.body: The boys describe riding to the mill behind Gluglu during their stay in Iberville. The passage does not establish whether this is a person or an animal.

introduction.name: The Pontelliers

snapshots.name: The Lebruns
snapshots.subtitle: The family that runs the Grand Isle cottages
snapshots.body: Madame Lebrun and her sons Robert and Victor. Their father died early in their parents’ marriage.
